name: Technique - Operator harmonics and filter
description: Standalone technique from the Ableton Operator checklist: drawn harmonics, filter distortion, velocity-to-filter, FM algorithms and resampling.

manual.instruction: Start with an Operator bass note and roll off the sub with Multiband Dynamics so the synth does not fight the kick or dedicated sub.
manual.verify: The bass has midrange weight without a bloated low end.
manual.why: dnksaus starts with multiband compression and turns off the sub band.

manual.instruction: Draw random harmonics in the oscillator until the waveform looks interesting. Shape it with the filter distortion and map velocity to filter frequency.
manual.verify: Harder notes open the filter and the bass responds to playing strength.
manual.why: dnksaus draws harmonics, uses filter distortion and assigns velocity to filter frequency.

manual.instruction: Use Operator's envelope and LFO on pitch, volume or filter, and try different FM algorithms and oscillator waveforms.
manual.verify: The patch has controlled movement and a distinct FM character.
manual.why: dnksaus demonstrates Operator's LFO, envelopes and FM algorithms.

manual.instruction: Add an Auto Filter in band-pass after Operator, map it to a macro, then resample the result to audio.
manual.verify: The same patch works as a full bass and a narrower filtered fill.
manual.why: dnksaus maps Auto Filter band-pass to a macro and resamples the Operator bass.

notes: Source: dnksaus, 'Make HEAVY Dubstep Basses with Operator' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PFmBcZujMwk). Transcript summary, not quotes. Reference-only because the engine cannot create or verify Operator patches.
